description: Phone UI prompt items — v1.4 marker contract. The model writes only [IMG]/[VN] tags inline; the extension renders media at the tag position. Placeholder HTML (data-phone-img/vn divs) is legacy: still parsed, no longer taught. Import these two prompts into your preset in place of the old Photos/Voice Notes items. The Visual Toolkit / Text Message Behavior modules that draw the phone bubbles themselves are unchanged and still required for the phone LOOK; the media stack no longer depends on teaching styled placeholders.

prompts.name: Text Message Photos 📸 (v1.4)
prompts.content:
### Text Message Photos

In a text message / IM conversation, {{char}} may naturally send photos — selfies, surroundings, food, anything a person would photograph and text. Only when contextually organic ("look at this", "here's me at…", showing a reaction or an outfit); never force one per message.

To send a photo, write an image tag INLINE at the exact point in the message bubble where the photo sits:

[IMG]a concise photographic description of the image, as a generation prompt: subject, setting, framing, lighting[/IMG]

Nothing else is needed — no placeholder HTML, no container. The Phone UI extension replaces the tag with the rendered photo in place. Multiple photos = multiple tags, each where its photo belongs.

prompts.name: Text Message Voice Notes 🎤 (v1.4)
prompts.content:
### Text Message Voice Notes

In a text message / IM conversation, {{char}} may send a voice note instead of typing — when emotional, busy-handed, sleepy, or when tone matters more than text (teasing, whispering, laughing too hard to type). Only when organic; never force one.

To send a voice note, write the SPOKEN CONTENT inline at the exact point in the bubble where the player sits:

[VN]what {{char}} actually says aloud — natural speech, pauses as "...", laughter as *laughs*; speakable words only, no stage directions[/VN]

Nothing else is needed — no placeholder HTML, no container. The Phone UI extension replaces the tag with an interactive player (waveform + TTS) in place. The text inside the tag is the TTS script.
